articles.title: How Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman turned red-eye flights and conflicting schedules into the unlikely foundation of a winning relationship
articles.summary: International Sports News: Tennis star Ben Shelton is having the best year of his career. He is in the US Open semi-finals, ranked No. 9 in the world, and has already collected .
articles.body: Tennis star Ben Shelton is having the best year of his career. He is in the US Open semi-finals, ranked No. 9 in the world, and has already collected titles in Montreal, Munich, Dallas, and Stuttgart in 2026. Behind that run is a partnership with Washington Spirit forward and two-time Olympic gold medalist Trinity Rodman that has grown as fast as his ranking. What makes it interesting is not the romance itself, but the specific, unglamorous lengths both have gone to for each other when their schedules collide.How did Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman start dating?Rodman made the first move, sending Shelton an Instagram DM that simply said "You're sick," accompanied by a fire emoji. Shelton replied within ten minutes, telling her she had been "sick at the Olympics too." They met in person a week or two later, and by March 2025, they had made the relationship Instagram official.Rodman later called the whole thing "cringe" on a podcast. Speaking on the *Not Gonna Lie* podcast with Kylie Kelce, she laughed it off: "Everything I do is just embarrassing. I'm really embarrassed. I said 'You're sick, fire emoji'. That's it. It worked... he responded within 10 minutes, so I win!"What came next was less funny and more telling. "I fully committed to this guy that I didn't even meet yet, for him to stay at my house for the weekend," Rodman said. "It's actually crazy, it's insane, but it worked out." That willingness to just figure things out on the fly has become something of a theme for them.How do Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman manage their schedules?This is where most sports couples hit a wall. Two elite athletes, two separate leagues, two travel-heavy calendars with almost no natural overlap. Rodman plays for the Washington Spirit in the NWSL and represents the US Women's National Team. Shelton chases ATP ranking points across multiple continents from January to November. The math rarely works.But they make it work anyway. At the 2025 US Open, Shelton told the crowd during his on-court interview: "My girlfriend took the red-eye from California last night to be here." Less than a day earlier, Rodman had been on the opposite side of the country, playing for the Spirit against Bay FC. By the following afternoon, she was sitting with Shelton's family in New York.It is easy to gloss over how much effort that actually takes. She played a professional match, boarded an overnight flight, landed at 5am, and was sitting courtside before noon. Shelton noticed. He said afterwards: "2 days off. I have some free time. My girlfriend took the red-eye from California last night to be here." The crowd roared. But what stuck was the simplicity of it. No grand gesture, no social media build-up. She just showed up.Shelton has returned the favour in kind. After his first-round exit from Wimbledon in July 2026, he was soon back in the stands watching Rodman play for the Spirit. She scored a 94th-minute winner against Houston, then ran toward the stands to celebrate with Shelton with a kiss. One week down, the next one up. That rhythm is the relationship.Why does Ben Shelton say having Trinity Rodman as a partner matters?Shelton has been clear that what he values most is not the presence, but the understanding behind it. He told the ATP Tour: "It's very important I think, one, having my family in my corner, who have been super supportive my whole career, it's really important. And, two, having a partner, a girlfriend, who understands all the same things, knows when to support, what to say in tough moments — is selfless enough to be there for me in my moments and actually enjoy my big moments and vice versa — has been really cool."That word, selfless, keeps coming up. He told Us Weekly: "You gotta make sacrifices sometimes. It's just the life that we live. I think that you have to have two selfless people in a situation like this, and I think we have that."He also pointed to something deeper. "Her path to being a professional athlete and being one of the best soccer players in the world hasn't been easy and she's dealt with more adversity than me," Shelton said. "To see that, understand it with the unfiltered version of it has been eye opening for sure. It puts perspective on things in life and is just cool to see her make it to where she wanted to."Rodman missed significant time in 2025 with chronic back pain, going on indefinite medical leave before fighting her way back to the pitch. Shelton had a front-row seat for all of it. "It was tough to watch last year, her being in pain, just doing everyday stuff, living life and not even taking soccer into account," he said. Watching someone you care about grind through pain with no finish line in sight changes how you see your own bad days on court. Shelton has said as much.How has Trinity Rodman supported Ben Shelton publicly?She has not been subtle about it. Rodman wore a T-shirt reading "I ♥️ MY BOYFRIEND" during Shelton's second-round match at the 2026 US Open. She has also shown up to smaller ATP events that most partners skip entirely. Unlike many who only attend Grand Slams, Rodman supported Shelton at ATP events in Stuttgart and Dallas in the lead-up to the US Open.Then there was the press conference moment. After a Washington Spirit match in September 2025, Shelton picked up a microphone and started interviewing Rodman himself. She reportedly could not stop laughing. It was the kind of thing that does not need any explanation. He showed up, made her laugh, and went home."It's funny because she's really gotten into tennis the way that I've gotten into soccer," Shelton said. "She's watching it all the time. Sometimes I'll go home, and she will have YouTube on, watching one of my old matches." That detail probably says more about where they are than any post-match interview.What makes their relationship different from other sports couples?Most high-profile athlete relationships exist largely in public-facing moments: the courtside appearances, the Instagram posts, the post-match mentions. Shelton and Rodman have all of that. But the more specific moments, the 5am arrivals, the press conference interviews, the immediate appearance at her NWSL game after Wimbledon ended early, point to something that functions differently in practice.Both of them understand the specific weight of competing under national expectation. Shelton is trying to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam since Andy Roddick in 2003. Rodman is one of the most scrutinised players in women's soccer, carrying both her own ambitions and the considerable weight of her famous surname. They are not just supporting each other. They are watching each other carry real pressure, up close, and choosing to stay present anyway.That, more than the matching custom outfits or the fire emoji origin story, is what makes this particular sports relationship worth paying attention to.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Sophie Cunningham built her $3 million net worth with a $665,000 WNBA salary and major endorsements

articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has turned her WNBA career into something much bigger than basketball. Since entering the league in 2019, the Indiana Fever guard has steadily increased her earnings while building a strong presence across endorsements, social media and media projects. Her move to Indiana in 2025 gave her another platform, and by 2026, Cunningham’s career earnings, brand deals and growing popularity had made her financial story worth a closer look.Sophie Cunningham’s net worth and WNBA career earningsCunningham’s estimated net worth is around $3 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. Her WNBA earnings have also climbed significantly during her career.Spotrac lists her career on-court earnings at more than $1.33 million since she entered the league. Her financial progress is especially notable when compared with her early seasons. Phoenix selected Cunningham in the second round of the 2019 WNBA Draft, and she initially signed a four-year contract worth nearly $190,000.After that first deal, her contracts gradually improved. She signed a one-year extension worth $75,000 in 2022 before agreeing to a two-year, $304,500 contract with Phoenix the following year. In September 2024, she signed another one-year extension worth $100,000.The biggest jump came after her move to Indiana. Her $665,000 base salary in 2026 is almost twice what she earned across her first seven seasons, according to the figures cited by Athlon Sports.That increase reflects the changing economics of the WNBA, but it also highlights Cunningham’s growing value as a player and personality.Her role changed after joining the Fever. Rather than serving primarily as a starter, she became an important sixth-woman option. In 2025, she averaged 8.6 points per game while shooting a career-best 46.9% from the field across 30 appearances.Sophie Cunningham’s endorsements and media empire add to her wealthCunningham’s income extends well beyond her WNBA salary. According to Booking Agent Info, she had at least nine active endorsement partnerships as of August 2026.Her brand portfolio includes adidas, while she also worked with European Wax Center in 2026. She previously landed an Arby’s endorsement in 2025. These partnerships have benefited from Cunningham’s growing visibility, both on the court and online.Her social media following has become another valuable asset. Cunningham reportedly has more than 8 million followers across Instagram, TikTok, X and Facebook. A following of that size can create additional opportunities through sponsored content and brand collaborations.She has also expanded into entertainment and sports media. Cunningham launched the “Show Me Something” podcast in 2025 with reality star West Wilson. The show has surpassed 60,000 YouTube subscribers and is produced by Colin Cowherd’s media company, The Volume, with Hard Rock BET as its presenting sponsor.Her profile grew again in 2026 when she appeared as a Sports Illustrated Swimsuit model and joined USA Network as a WNBA studio analyst and contributor.Cunningham’s journey began long before the spotlight of the Indiana Fever. At the University of Missouri, she became a standout player and earned SEC Freshman of the Year honors. She later collected first-team All-SEC recognition during each of her final three college seasons.Now, her career combines basketball, endorsements, media and fashion. The result is a business profile that continues to grow alongside her WNBA career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham drops candid reaction to ‘s*x symbol’ perception around her name: “That is way better”
articles.summary: International Sports News: Sophie Cunningham has never appeared interested in fitting the usual image of a WNBA player. The Indiana Fever guard has been open about her personali.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham has never appeared interested in fitting the usual image of a WNBA player. The Indiana Fever guard has been open about her personality, her fashion choices, and her willingness to answer difficult questions without much hesitation. During a recent conversation with Colin Cowherd, Cunningham found herself facing a label that often follows athletes who attract attention outside the court. Her reaction was not defensive. Instead, she laughed it off and made it clear she was comfortable with how she presents herself.Sophie Cunningham reacts to 's*x symbol' perceptionDuring an appearance on Colin Cowherd's Volume podcast network, Sophie Cunningham was asked about how she is viewed within the WNBA. Cowherd began describing her place in the league before pausing. "You are kind of viewed as the leagues…ummm," Cowherd hesitated."Just say it," Cunningham interrupted."S*x symbol," he responded."That is way better, I thought you were gonna go somewhere completely different," she responded jokingly.Cunningham later explained why she has no problem embracing a more feminine image while playing professional basketball. For her, fashion and competitiveness have never been mutually exclusive."For me, the reason why I really lean into that is, first of all, I've always been super girly. Since a little girl, I've always loved to dress up. I love dresses. I love high heels. I love all of that," Cunningham explained.The Fever guard continued, "For some reason, our society, if you play basketball, you can't dress that way, or you can't be girly. No one's ever said it, but it's like, they kind of feel like you can't be both. Screw all that. Yes, you can. You can be girly, and you can go out and kick someone's a*s."Sophie Cunningham launches new podcastCunningham has also added another outlet for those conversations with the launch of "No Hesitation," a podcast she hosts with basketball trainer Drew Hanlen. The show debuted Thursday and replaces "Show Me Something," her previous podcast with West Wilson.The new program is centered on basketball and the personalities surrounding the sport. Cunningham said she wanted a platform where conversations could be more direct."I just felt like there was not a podcast or really any social media out there that gave you real, honest truth about basketball and strictly basketball," Cunningham said.Hanlen also addressed the gap between Cunningham's actual comments and the way some of them are portrayed online."People think you’re like some troll and make statements, but really it’s 99% of the time people ask you a question, you answer, you give your opinion, and then people blow it up and act like you made a big political statement," Hanlen said."Stop asking me questions if you don’t want the truth," Cunningham responded.Cunningham used the debut episode to discuss several basketball-related topics, including media coverage and recognition within the WNBA. She argued that popularity and politics can sometimes influence award voting."I think it’s very political. I think there’s a lot of people who are really, really great who don’t get the credit because maybe they don’t have the popularity or they don’t have the platform," Cunningham said.She also called on the league's media to focus more closely on what is happening on the court."I think you kind of hit it when you said the WNBA media pretty much covers everything but basketball," Cunningham said.Cunningham believes the league is entering an important period, with the WNBA expanding and a new commissioner set to take over after Cathy Engelbert's planned departure at the end of 2026. She said better practice facilities should be a basic priority for every franchise.The podcast is scheduled to release new episodes each Thursday, with Cunningham promising a mix of film study, strategy and candid discussion around professional basketball.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Indian people always very interested in what we do': Alireza Firouzja, youngest to beat Magnus Carlsen's 2800 record | Exclusive
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: A 22-year-old grandmaster, one of the strongest players on the planet, lying flat on a hotel bed with his leg propped up on a pillow, calcu.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A 22-year-old grandmaster, one of the strongest players on the planet, lying flat on a hotel bed with his leg propped up on a pillow, calculating variations against a World Championship challenger sitting upright across the board. That was Alireza Firouzja's reality for a stretch of tournaments earlier this year, a fallout from an ankle injury. It was surreal."I just stepped wrongly," Firouzja, now 23, told TimesofIndia.com, recalling the moment that caught the chess world's attention during the Super Chess Classic in Bucharest, Romania, earlier this year in May. "I wanted to come down from the stage, and I stepped wrongly, and I twisted my ankle."Just a wrong step off a stage, except this time it happened to someone with a full tournament calendar and no real option to simply rest up.The injury first sidelined his movement during the Grand Chess Tour leg in Romania, which he described as the low point of the entire saga. "Romania was the most annoying part, because I had to lie on the bed and keep the feet up," he added.Things improved slightly by the time he reached Norway Chess, where he was on crutches but was at least able to sit behind the board again."In Norway already I could sit behind the table," he said. But Romania was the stretch that tested him most. Among those opponents was Javokhir Sindarov, now the World Championship challenger who will face Gukesh later this year.Asked directly what it actually felt like, calculating chess from a horizontal position, leg elevated, unable to sit up properly, he didn't hide his annoyance."It was very unpleasant," he revealed. " But I just wanted to play, because it was a good opportunity. But after two rounds, I just said, it's enough. It was impossible to play."He's since made a full recovery. "It's fully recovered," he confirmed.Back in India, and clearly enjoying itThe bed-and-pillow chapter is behind him, but Firouzja's relationship with Indian crowds has become one of the more consistent threads of his year.This is his second trip to the country in the space of three to four months. He won the Chennai Grand Masters tournament in July before arriving for the Global Chess League (GCL) here in Bengaluru, where he plays for two-time champions Triveni Continental Kings."India, always, whenever I come, people are very interested in what we do, and it's very good," he said, when asked about the reception. "I've been this year two times already, I was in Chennai, now here, and last year I was in Mumbai (for GCL)."The food, apparently, has made an impression too. Revealing what he enjoys the most, Firouzja said, "I like the chicken tandoori and stuff."On Gukesh vs SindarovWith Sindarov set to challenge Gukesh for the World Championship, Firouzja, who has played both multiple times in different formats of the game so far, offered his assessment of the upcoming clash in Geneva."I think it will be a close match, probably," he added. "I don't know, anything could happen."Alireza, an Iranian-French grandmaster, became the youngest player to surpass a FIDE rating of 2800, achieving it at 18 years and 5 months in November 2021, breaking Magnus Carlsen’s previous record of 18 years and 11 months.Despite achieving so much at a young age, he was more expansive on just how hard the road to World Championship match actually is, having walked much of it himself."You have to play a lot, and you have to always be in your best shape," he said of qualifying through the Candidates Tournament. "And Candidates, in these two weeks, you have to play your best. It's a hard journey. It's good to try."What's next for Firouzja?As for where he heads after GCL, Firouzja confirmed his next major stop remains the Total Chess Championship, which is set to be held from November 10 to 21, 2026, at the Anantara New York Palace Hotel in Budapest, Hungary.Between a freak ankle injury, a full recovery, two trips to India in under half a year, a taste for tandoori chicken, and a top-level chess schedule, the image that will stick, though, is the one from Romania.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "It's going to be challenging": Max Verstappen reveals his surprising plan for a crazy 100-driver challenge at Silverstone
articles.summary: International Sports News: Max Verstappen is preparing for one of the most unusual racing challenges of his career, and his approach could not be more relaxed. The four-time For.
articles.body: Max Verstappen is preparing for one of the most unusual racing challenges of his career, and his approach could not be more relaxed. The four-time Formula 1 champion will start from the back of a 100-driver karting field at Silverstone and try to overtake every competitor within 30 laps. The event will bring together athletes, streamers, content creators, personalities and fans, creating a very different racing environment from a Formula 1 Grand Prix. While many drivers might study their rivals before such a challenge, Max Verstappen has chosen not to. Instead, he plans to arrive, race and deal with whatever happens on the track.Max Verstappen plans to simply show up and race 100 drivers without doing any special preparationThe biggest surprise surrounding Max Verstappen's Silverstone challenge is not only the number of competitors. It is how little preparation he has done for the event.A normal Formula 1 weekend gives drivers plenty of information before they race. Teams study opponents, analyze track data and prepare for different situations. Max Verstappen will have none of that same structure when he lines up behind 100 go-karters.The Dutch driver admitted that he has not researched the people he will face."No, I didn't do anything," Max Verstappen said when asked if he had looked up his competitors.Max Verstappen then made it clear that he intends to treat the event as something to enjoy rather than another highly controlled race weekend."I'll just rock up and have a good time, to be honest. Let's see how it goes. But yeah, it's a lot of people."That relaxed attitude does not mean the challenge will be simple. Starting at the back means Max Verstappen will have to work through traffic almost immediately. With 100 karts sharing the circuit, finding clean space and choosing the right moment to pass could become a major part of the test.Max Verstappen also does not yet know exactly how the event will work."Starting from the back, it's going to be challenging, but I hope I can catch them all. But we don't know yet. I don't even know the format at the moment. So I will just rock up and do my thing."For a driver known for his aggressive racecraft and quick decisions, the event could become a test of instinct more than preparation.Charles Leclerc warns Max Verstappen about the huge field while Carlos Sainz expects him to reach the front with easeMax Verstappen's Formula 1 rivals have already offered their thoughts on the unusual challenge, with Charles Leclerc focusing on the risks created by such a large field."I mean, 100 is a lot," Charles Leclerc said.The Ferrari driver joked that competitors should avoid crashing into Max Verstappen, especially because the Red Bull Racing driver still has a Formula 1 season to finish. Charles Leclerc also questioned how experienced some of the participants might be compared with a professional Formula 1 driver.Carlos Sainz was even more confident about Max Verstappen's chances.Carlos Sainz recently competed in a karting race where he started 20th because of a reverse-grid format. He said he reached first place within five laps, giving him a simple way to estimate how quickly Max Verstappen could move through the Silverstone field."I did a karting race yesterday with my team. Started 20th because we did reverse grid and I was P1 in five laps. So by my calculations, if there are another 20 times five, in 20 laps Max will be P1 for sure. 15-20 laps, or who knows, depends how much overtaking there is. But he will win it easy."Carlos Sainz's prediction adds confidence to the idea that Max Verstappen could reach the front well before the 30-lap limit. Still, the 100-driver field introduces an element of uncertainty that cannot be measured through normal Formula 1 experience.For Max Verstappen, that appears to be exactly what makes the event interesting. He will have speed and experience on his side, but the crowded track, unknown competitors and unusual format could make the challenge unlike anything he faces during a Formula 1 weekend.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Global Chess League: Magnus Carlsen gets better of Sindarov
articles.summary: Chess News: Bengaluru: Two-time champions Triveni Continental Kings, who featured in the finals of all the three previous editions of the Global Chess League (GCL.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Two-time champions Triveni Continental Kings, who featured in the finals of all the three previous editions of the Global Chess League (GCL), crashed out of the fourth edition on Friday. They remained at the bottom of the standings in the six-team league.Led by Alireza Firouzja, the youngest player to reach Elo rating of 2800 in 2021, the Kings were expected to put up another spirited fight but they lost their way early in the Garden City. On Friday, they took down the V Anand-led PBG Alaskan Knights 13-7 which ensured the Knights also went out of the reckoning.The win, powered by the women - Zhu Jiner and Alexandra Kosteniuk - together with Pranav Venkatesh on the prodigy board, was only their third in nine matches which sealed their fate. Last season, the Kings won eight out of their 10 matches.CheQ Mumbai Masters (12 match-points), with Maxime Vachier-Lagrave on the icon board, are also out of the final reckoning. Ganges Grandmasters, Alpine AL Pipers (18 each) and Fyres American Gambits (15) are the only three teams remaining in contention. The top-two teams make it to the Sunday's two-set final after Saturday's last day of the league phase.Carlsen beats SindarovWorld No. 1 Magnus Carlsen began to shift gears as the tournament neared the business end. He took down world championship challenger Javokhir Sindarov with white pieces that helped Alpine Pipers edge Fyers American Gambits 9-7. Carlsen gave away his Player of the Match award to teammate Vidit Gujrathi after the latter defeated the Norwegian's former second Daniil Dubov of Russia.Pipers are now level with Grandmasters but dropped to second with 82 game-points compared to Ganges' 88. Ganges stormed to the top of the table after thrashing Mumba Masters 16-1.Margins are small: Van WelyKings' coach Loek van Wely was at a loss for words. He told TOI, "It's really hard to say (now) what went wrong. We need to evaluate when the dust settles, we need to analyze. "Against Ganges (Grandmasters), we should have won both matches. Sometimes, the margin is very small. The match can look very good and then in the final two minutes everything will change. The higher the level, the differences are getting smaller."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A century crossed, more ahead: India eye greater continental glory at Asian Games 2026
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: On a crisp March afternoon in 1951, inside the newly christened National Stadium in New Delhi, an infant republic dared to dream in broad daylight.Bar.
articles.body: On a crisp March afternoon in 1951, inside the newly christened National Stadium in New Delhi, an infant republic dared to dream in broad daylight.Barely four years removed from the trauma of Partition and the dawn of Independence, India did not merely host the inaugural Asian Games, she breathed life into it.Under the motto ‘Ever Onward’, a fledgling nation gathered eleven Asian delegations to celebrate sport, brotherhood and human endurance.When Sachin Nag surged through the water to claim 100m freestyle gold, and Lavy Pinto blazed across the newly built cinder track to complete a historic sprint double (100m and 200m), sport became something far larger than podium finishes. It was an affirmation of identity. It was a statement to the world that India, long silenced, had arrived to run, leap and fight on her own terms.Yet, the decades that followed were not an unbroken march of success. For generations of Indian sports lovers, the Asian Games became an exercise in poetic longing, a canvas marked by solitary bursts of genius amid systemic heartbreaks.We held tight to those incandescent moments. We remembered the peerless stride of ‘Flying Sikh’ Milkha Singh in Tokyo in 1958 where he won the 200m and 400m gold, the sheer, indomitable spirit of PT Usha storming the track in Seoul in 1986 with four gold medals fluttering against her chest, and the bruising, pride-drenched clashes of our hockey teams on natural turf and synthetic pitch alike.These were beacons in the dark, but the broader arithmetic remained modest. For years, the continent’s tally hovered in the twenties, thirties and forties.Over seven decades, that ledger grew steadily but consistently. With a lifetime tally of 779 medals—consisting of 183 gold, 239 silver, and 357 bronze—this quiet record captures the essence of our athletic struggles and our unyielding drive.Then came 2022 Hangzhou, an edition delayed to 2023 by the Covid-19 pandemic.Something fundamental had shifted in the core of Indian sport. The diffidence of old had evaporated, replaced by an unapologetic, ruthless hunger. Before the contingent boarded their flights, an audacious phrase echoed through the corridors of training centres: “Iss baar, 100 paar.”To many, it sounded like wishful bravado. India had never achieved a 75-medal haul in a single edition, with their second-highest tally being 70 medals at Jakarta Games in 2018. A triple-digit haul was something expected only from traditional sporting powerhouses like China, Japan and South Korea, not a nation that had long carried the tag of an underachiever.What unfolded in Hangzhou was nothing short of an athletic revolution. Day after day, the national anthem played with relentless regularity. It was not just one discipline carrying the burden; it was a total, across-the-board breakthrough.In equestrian, four young riders ended a 41-year gold drought in dressage. At the shooting ranges, a new generation of marksmen competed with the composure of seasoned masters. The badminton courts, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty smashed through the traditional Chinese, Malaysian and Korean pairs to claim a historic men’s doubles crown. On the track, Neeraj Chopra won back-to-back Asian Games gold medals, while the nation celebrated the performances of its archers, wrestlers and athletes across disciplines.When the dust settled, the scoreboard bore testimony to history: 28 gold, 38 silver and 41 bronze. A total of 107 medals.India had not merely crossed a critical threshold; she had smashed through it, securing 4th place on the Asian Games table.The triple-digit barrier, that psychological ceiling that had constrained Indian ambitions for over seventy years, was shattered in pieces. Hangzhou was the turning point where Indian sport stopped knocking on the door of global elites and simply walked in.Now, the calendar has turned, and the countdown towards Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, has started.The emotional landscape of this upcoming campaign is entirely different. Hangzhou was about proving that India could; Aichi-Nagoya is about proving that Hangzhou was merely the foundation.The targets are no longer shrouded in modesty. The mandate for the Indian contingent heading to the Land of the Rising Sun is crystal clear: break into the continental top three.To stand shoulder-to-shoulder with China, Japan and South Korea demands an escalation in every single arena.More than that, Aichi-Nagoya is going to be an essential stepping stone towards the ultimate prize, the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. The battles fought on Japanese mats, tracks and courts will serve as the stress-test for Olympic destiny. The medals won will be the currency that’s going to fuel India’s LA 2028 campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: GCL: Ganges Grandmasters run riot on Day 7; Magnus Carlsen gives POTM trophy to Vidit Gujrathi
articles.summary: Chess News: BENGALURU: Ganges Grandmasters and defending champions APL Pipers strengthened their chances of reaching the Global Chess League final after convincin.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Ganges Grandmasters and defending champions APL Pipers strengthened their chances of reaching the Global Chess League final after convincing victories in the penultimate round of Season 4 in Bengaluru on Friday. Both teams now need just a win in their final round-robin match on Saturday to secure a place in the title clash.Ganges Grandmasters produced the biggest victory of the tournament, thrashing Mumba Masters 16-1, while the Pipers edged American Gambits 9-7 in a crucial battle between the top two teams.The results left Ganges and Pipers level on 18 match points, but Ganges moved into first place with 88 game points, four more than Pipers.The Pipers’ victory was highlighted by world No. 1 Magnus Carlsen ending Candidates 2026 winner Javokhir Sindarov’s three-game winning streak.While Divya Deshmukh’s difficult GCL debut continued as she ran out of time against Bibisara Assaubayeva, Carlsen controlled the Icon board encounter and forced Sindarov to resign after 36 moves.He was named Player of the Match but then handed the trophy to teammate Vidit Gujrathi, who sealed the match by defeating Daniil Dubov.Vidit prevailed in a marathon 96-move battle on the Superstar Men board, keeping his composure in a time scramble to convert an extra knight and pawn against Dubov’s rook.“First of all, I think this was a great match with a very good team performance. We are thrilled to get the win. In my game, I was doing pretty well early on, but he (Sindarov) put up a big fight but I was able to wriggle out and find the win,” Carlsen said, before giving the MOTM trophy to Vidit."I do not deserve this 'player of the match' as much as the man who won us the match," the five-time classical World Champion said, acknowledging Vidit's contribution.Ganges’ commanding victory was powered by Ian Nepomniachtchi, Levon Aronian, Leinier Dominguez Perez, Stavroula Tsolakidou and Leon Luke Mendonca, who all won their games with White. Polina Shuvalova drew with Harika, while the Mumba Masters endured a heavy defeat.In the day’s other match, Triveni Continental Kings defeated Alaskan Knights 13-7. Triveni's Zhu Jiner registered her first win of the tournament against Kateryna Lagno, Alexandra Kosteniuk beat Nino Batsiashvili, and Pranav Venkatesh defeated Abhimanyu Mishra. Meanwhile, Knights' Arjun Erigaisi also beat Wei Yi, while 15-year-old Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus defeated Aravindh Chithambaram. But those wins were not enough to take them home.Ganges and Pipers will qualify for the final with victories, while the Gambits need one of the top two teams to lose and must beat Mumba Masters by a convincing margin to keep their hopes alive.GCL 2026 Points table after Day 7Pos.TeamMPGP1Ganges Grandmasters18882APL Pipers18823American Gambits15804Mumba Masters12745Alaskan Knights9716Triveni Continental Kings970GCL 2026 fixtures for Day 8 - Saturday, September 125:00 PM: Triveni Continental Kings vs APL Pipers6:30 PM: Alaskan Knights vs Ganges Grandmasters8:00 PM: American Gambits vs Mumba MastersGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harry Kane admits he talked to Bayern Munich about extension this week
articles.summary: Kane on FC Bayern contract negotiations: “Right now I’m at a happy place.”
articles.body:
After Bayern Munich 's 5-0 win against Bodo/Glimt, goal scorer Harry Kane was asked about his ongoing contract negotiations with the club. Though he could not offer any details of the contract or when he expects it to be done, he spoke with a calm confidence that everything would get done in due time.

"We had conversations, a couple of weeks ago and some more this week. As I said before, a contract doesn't happen overnight — it takes time to digest and see how we can make it best case possible for everyone involved. I don't expect it to be done in the next week or two, but hopefully in the next one or two months we should be where we want to be. Right now I'm at a happy place. All I want to do and what the club wants me to do is to focus on the pitch, score the goals and help the team. I'm calm.. It's hard to talk to you guys about it because it's confidential stuff. I'm sure in due time you'll know about the details and get the answers you're looking for. All I can say now is that the conversations are going well. We'll see what happens," Kane said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia )

Kane's contract expires at the end of this season, but both sides seem to be confident that a deal will get done to keep the England captain in Bavaria. His comments on Thursday are consistent with updates from Bayern front office officials over the past months.

articles.title: "We are all in this together" – Marcel Schäfer sends clear message amid RB Leipzig criticism
articles.summary: After a promising start with two wins, RB Leipzig have suffered back-to-back defeats to Werder Bremen and Como, sparking significant criticism in the press a...
articles.body:
After a promising start with two wins, RB Leipzig have suffered back-to-back defeats to Werder Bremen and Como , sparking significant criticism in the press and on social media.

RB Leipzig managing director for sport Marcel Schäfer has now shared his thoughts on the situation, acknowledging that the team's recent performances have fallen well below expectations.

"We have, of course, seen what has been said about the club in the press and on social media over the past few days. We are highly ambitious, but we are also critical of ourselves. The last two results have not been good enough. We know that, and we are not going to sugar-coat it. We are addressing the situation very clearly internally," Schäfer said in a statement released by RB Leipzig on Friday night.

Despite the recent setbacks, Schäfer was keen to underline the club's full support for new head coach Martin Demichelis and his squad, stressing that, given the significant changes made at the club over the summer, it's only natural that the team will need time to fully gel.

"At the same time, we are staying calm and focused, and we are united as a club. That applies to everyone who works here, the players and the entire coaching staff. They all have our full support and trust," he said.

"We made a number of changes over the summer, brought new players into the squad and have also had several injuries to deal with. Important players are now coming back. A new-look team needs time to gel and to develop an understanding on the pitch. That is simply the reality.

"We believe in the quality of our squad and we know what this team is capable of. Now we need to learn the right lessons, continue to work hard and make progress over the coming weeks. We are all in this together, we share the responsibility and we will keep doing what we believe is right. We won't be distracted by what's being said."

With pressure mounting following the two heavy defeats, RB Leipzig will be determined to return to winning ways when they welcome bottom-placed Hamburger SV to the Red Bull Arena on Sunday.

articles.title: 'You do feel like a pop star' - Stephen Bunting on his viral walk-on
articles.summary: From local pubs to sell-out arenas, Stephen "The Bullet" Bunting talks about his incredible darts journey.
articles.body:
Stephen "The Bullet" Bunting's love for darts was formed at a young age while watching his dad play at their local pub.

"I think I was about 12 or 13," he remembered. "Hood up, sneaking around, sitting at the back, being very quiet with a bag of crisps and a fizzy orange."

Nearly three decades later, and now a father himself, everything has gone full circle for Fazakerley's finest.

His elder son now watches him play... albeit in sold-out arenas across the country rather than in their local boozer.

"In darts, if it goes wrong there's only you that can change it," said the 41-year-old Bunting, who now lives in St Helens.

"But no matter who's in the audience... I hear [my son's] voice above anyone else, even if there's 20,000 in the crowd.

"I'll hear him shouting me, geeing me up.

"I think that's the most important thing - to try and stay positive."

Bunting's walk-on routine ahead of his matches features David Guetta and Sia's hit Titanium.

It often goes viral on social media and never fails to get the crowd singing along.

"It's amazing to be honest," said Bunting. "You do feel like a pop star.

As a teenager, Bunting won the British Teenage Open and World Youth Masters titles before making his BDO [British Dart Organisation] World Championship debut aged only 18.

Since then, Bunting has amassed more than 30 regional and national titles in addition to his multiple professional tournament wins.

He has witnessed how the game has captured the attention of much bigger audiences in recent years, in large part thanks to another teenage sensation from the North West, Luke Littler.

"It's crazy to think that all them years ago when I was playing the BDO, there was people in the front row doing some knitting," he said.

"It was crazy and now you've people throwing beers in the air at £8 a pint.

"Just a really party, carnival atmosphere. Everyone enjoys the darts."

Bunting's life story has now been turned into a book - Bulletproof: From Pub to Palace, My Life in Darts.

"It's a dream come true to be honest," he said.

"I never thought that I would have had a book out, especially when I first started playing."

articles.title: Titans Claim $2 Million O-Lineman Off Waivers Before Season Opener
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans claimed an offensive lineman off the waiver wire just a couple of days before the season opener The post Titans Claim $2 Million O-Linem...
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are bolstering the offensive line just ahead of the season opener against the New York Jets .

According to Titans senior writer Jim Wyatt, the Titans have claimed guard Atonio Mafi off waivers.

"The @Titans have claimed OL Atonio Mafi off waivers. The Titans have waived OL Garrett Dellinger ."

Mafi, a fifth-round selection in the 2023 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots , will be on his fourth team in four seasons. The guard last played 23 games in his career, started seven, and most recently played for the Las Vegas Raiders .

The offensive lineman has recorded around $2 million in career earnings since entering the league in 2023.

To make room for Mafi, the Titans waived Garrett Dellinger , a former 2025 seventh-round draft pick by the Baltimore Ravens . The guard made his professional debut with the Cleveland Browns , playing once.

Now, the former 243rd overall selection will have to find his potential fourth team in two seasons.

The 2026 season is a big season for quarterback Cam Ward .

While Ward put up decent numbers in his rookie season, the first overall pick of the 2025 draft didn't quite meet the expectations set on him.

Now under the tutelage of offensive coordinator Brian Daboll, the 2026 season will be big for the QB. But it all starts with the offensive line, as it was a big issue for Ward last season.

The former Miami Hurricane was taken down 55 times in his rookie season, tied for the most in the league alongside Geno Smith .

With head coach Robert Saleh and Daboll now in the circle with Ward, they will do their best to protect the young quarterback.

Ward has mentioned the new offensive system has allowed him to be "himself," which could be a big benefit ahead of his second season and prevent him from being sacked as often in 2026.

"I think I'm way more intelligent in terms of an NFL game," Ward said, via the Tennessean . "I think playing on time is a big factor that's been successful on offense. I think the more I can do that, the more it's going to put myself and this offense in a successful situation."

"They allow me to be myself… Upstairs and downstairs. The new system we're in is more of my style. Coach Dabs is a big part of that. And I think the entire offensive and defensive staff, they don't try to change the person or anything. Just be yourself."

While Atonio Mafi will be a depth piece for the Titans in his tenure, depending on how long that is, he could provide some protection for Ward if one of the starters goes down with an injury.

Robert Saleh Explains How to Start Titans Tenure

Robert Saleh will enter his first season as head coach with the Tennessee Titans, his second head coaching job after the NY Jets.

The Titans ended the 2025 season with a 3-14 record, with Saleh hoping the team starts off the season with a win.

"I would speak for all 32 teams that winning Week 1, starting fast, is always good," Saleh said, via Sports Illustrated . "You never know… You win a couple early, starting getting momentum, start getting confidence with a young group, who knows where it goes?"

If the Titans win, it would be a perfect start to the Saleh era, who would win against his former employer.

articles.title: Giants' bid for fourth straight win done in by Padres' fast start
articles.summary: The Giants, the one team in the majors without a four-game winning streak, had a chance to change that Friday but fell into a 7-1 hole and could not turn thi...
articles.body:
Any anticipation that the San Francisco Giants might win four games in a row for the first time this year seemingly dissipated by the third inning Friday night until a two-out threat made things much more interesting in the ninth.

And yet, no dice. The Padres' early outburst held up, leaving the Giants with still a vague chance to lose 100 games while highlighting the team's astonishing inability to sustain success. Adding an extra touch of melancholy, Robbie Ray , an All-Star with San Francisco last year, was the Padres' starting pitcher, and while he gave up Rafael Devers ' 36th homer, a grand slam in the fifth, the Giants never got closer in a 7-5 loss at Oracle Park.

San Francisco went down fighting though, putting two on with two outs in the ninth against All-Star closer Mason Miller , a gorgeous bunt base hit by Jonah Cox bringing up Devers. "I mean the guts to put down that bunt is one thing, but the execution is another," manager Tony Vitello marveled.

Miller pitched Devers carefully - Vitello noted that it would have been easy for Devers to hack at three pitches to try to be the hero, but he selflessly took what he was given. He walked to load the bases, a scenario Bryce Eldridge enjoys, but Miller got Eldridge looking at a 103 mph pitch at the bottom of the zone to end the game.

"I thought the ninth was great, to get back into the fight," Vitello said. "In a baseball game that's 7-1, you're kind of on the outside looking in, and you want to be in the thick of things, and that's where we got."

E: Marte (1). LOB: San Diego 9, San Francisco 7. 2B: Merrill (24), Fermin 2 (13), Campusano (12), Bogaerts (15), Knizner (3), Eldridge (22). 3B: D.Harris (2), Tatis (3). HR: Devers (36), off Ray. RBIs: D.Harris 2 (8), Fermin 2 (19), Campusano (28), Bogaerts 2 (54), Eldridge (53), Devers 4 (96). SB: Cox (10), Merrill (26), Taylor (8).

Runners left in scoring position: San Diego 6 (Campusano, Bogaerts, Cronenworth 3, Tatis); San Francisco 4 (Gilbert, Whitcomb, Eldridge 2). RISP: San Diego 6 for 18; San Francisco 2 for 9.

ABS Challenge: Marte (Ball-Confirmed); Harris (Strike-Confirmed); Fermin (Strike-Confirmed); Basabe (Strike-Overturned to Ball); Gilbert (Strike-Overturned to Ball); Miller (Ball-Confirmed); Eldridge (Strike-Confirmed).

Umpires: Home, Stu Scheuwater; First, Jordan Baker; Second, Junior Valentine; Third, Rob Drake.

There's value, too, in making the Padres use their top three relievers in a game that looked like a romp initially. Giants starter Anthony Molina, very good in his first three starts since being acquired from Atlanta for Tyler Mahle on Aug. 3, didn't have it. He was throwing plenty of strikes, the emphasis for a pitching staff that has struggled, but they were getting drilled. Molina allowed nine hits, including five doubles and a triple, and seven runs in his three innings.

"I think what happened is I was missing the outside strike zone," Molina said, with Erwin Higueros interpreting. He speculated he was flying open a little too much with his changeup, giving up three hits on that pitch.

With few certainties about the Giants' rotation next year, Molina and Yunior Marte , who took over in the fourth, are trying to stake claims now. So too is lefty César Perdomo , who is scheduled to start Saturday against the Padres.

Molina, 24, vaulted to the top of the consideration list with his 3-0 record and 1.88 ERA in his first three starts, something of surprise given he was used in relief during his previous callups with the Rockies and Braves. In the minors, he mostly started.

Marte, 23, has made just one start but he has turned in strong work, with a 2.45 ERA. Take notice: He gave up a leadoff triple to Fernando Tatis Jr. in the eighth, then retired Jake Cronenworth , Manny Machado (strikeout) and Luis Campusano . Opponents are batting .189 against Marte.

Heading into 2027, the Giants have only two settled spots in the rotation, with Logan Webb and Landen Roupp . Hayden Birdsong could be back from Tommy John surgery close to the start of the season but he's not an automatic for the rotation or even a big-league spot immediately.

With looming labor strife, it's unclear if San Francisco will pursue any major free agents, but should the team do so, a solid veteran starter would be advisable - maybe a Robbie Ray type, assuming the Tarik Skubal-level free agents are out of reach. Either way, there will be one or two rotation spots still to fill and Molina, Marte and Perdomo essentially are getting early looks.

Devers got a day off Wednesday, ending his games played streak at 309, and the team was off Thursday, so the slugger was well rested. He golfed a low knuckle-curve from Ray, not a bad pitch at all, out to right.

"That's the very definition of a basic concept that's hard to do: Just stay to the ball," Vitello said, "That is a picture perfect example we could use in spring training."

Devers' 96 RBIs are the most by a Giants player since Hunter Pence 's 99 in 2013.

San Francisco would love to trip up San Diego, a division rival currently in the NL's final wild-card spot after the Giants swept the Cardinals this week.

"Looking ahead of the schedule and the time of year, by nature, there's going to be certain teams that are clawing for that," Vitello said of facing wild-card hopefuls while adding his own team is "kind of caught up in what they got going on and trying to build relationships and find their personality a little bit."

Every other team has won four consecutive games at some point. It's not much of an accomplishment, but San Francisco just can't get there, even with a young group that has played with determination

articles.title: Frederick Keys process abrupt season-ending loss to Greensboro in back-and-forth divisional finale
articles.summary: The crowd’s voice rose for Jaiden Lo Re. The 19-year-old, in just his third week of High-A baseball, had the Frederick Keys’ season on his bat. He battled to...
articles.body:
The crowd's voice rose for Jaiden Lo Re.

The 19-year-old, in just his third week of High-A baseball, had the Frederick Keys' season on his bat. He battled to a full count and stroked a fly ball to straightaway center field.

The voices rose a little higher. His Frederick teammates kept faith that this ball would find a way to the ground and kickstart another ninth-inning comeback bid for the second straight night.

But the ball found leather. It smacked into the glove of a waiting Edward Florentino, who set off a raucous Greensboro Grasshoppers celebration in the middle of Nymeo Field at Harry Grove Stadium.

The Keys watched the whole thing, lingering at the top step of the dugout as they processed the 7-5 loss in a winner-take-all Game 3 of the South Atlantic League North Division Series that abruptly concluded one of the best seasons in club history.

"It was a crazy back and forth, super emotional game," Frederick manager Collin Woody said. "We really genuinely didn't ever feel like we were out of it at any moment in the game until the center fielder caught the ball."

As the Grasshoppers gave celebratory hugs to all who crossed their path, the Keys shared embraces of condolence. They were for all: coaches, staff and upper management that came to the clubhouse for the last time in 2026.

Instead of playing for its first championship since Frederick won the Carolina League in 2011, the players prepared to depart.

"It's bittersweet, obviously," Keys catcher Ryan Stafford said. "It didn't end the way that we wanted it to, but there's so much more to take away from this year. The way we fought for one another, the love that we had in the clubhouse. … We don't want to leave it on a sad note like this."

That camaraderie powered Frederick all season in its return to affiliated baseball with the Baltimore Orioles , and it was nearly enough to power past heavyweight Greensboro in a battle between two of the minor leagues' top squads record-wise.

There were three ties and four lead changes Friday as the game seesawed in each team's favor.

The Keys' pitching had largely done enough to hold down the Grasshoppers' potent lineup, which averaged 6.8 runs per game during the regular season, in the first two games. It appeared to do so again as Frederick gave the ball to two of its top relievers to protect a 5-4 lead entering the eighth inning.

But Florentino cranked a leadoff home run to even the contest and touch up Keys right-hander Twine Palmer, who had pitched three perfect innings prior to that blast. Greensboro then scrapped together one baserunner after another against Frederick southpaw Braeden Sloan before breaking through in the bottom third of the order on Brent Iredale's RBI single.

"We felt good about how we had everything lined up," Woody said. "It's just one of those matchups where two really good teams go at each other. A big strength of ours down the stretch has been our pitching, and a big strength of theirs all year was their offense. And tonight, they beat us."

The Grasshoppers' Wyatt Sanford led off the game with a first-pitch home run, the first of two solo shots as part of a three-hit night. Josh Tate knocked a go-ahead two-run single up the middle in the fourth inning, and Dylan Palmer plated their final run for insurance in the eighth.

The Keys' Ty Head laid down a successful squeeze bunt in the first to plate Enddy Azocar. Lo Re also hustled home with the tying run in the fifth. Stafford and Yasmil Bucce each singled in a run in the second inning, and Andrés Nolaya blasted a pinch-hit home run to lead off the sixth and send his side in front for the final time.

Treyson Peters earned the win for the Grasshoppers with two innings of scoreless, one-hit relief. He struck out three. Palmer took the loss for Frederick.

Greensboro, the Pittsburgh Pirates ' High-A affiliate, advanced to face in-state rival Winston-Salem in the South Atlantic League Championship Series, which begins Sunday.
authors: Alexander Dacy, The Frederick News-Post, Md.

Ben Shelton reached his first career Grand Slam final on Friday night, but the 23-year-old made clear afterward that holding his focus inside Arthur Ashe Stadium was its own battle. Speaking on court following his 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 win over fellow American Frances Tiafoe , Shelton admitted the celebrity-packed crowd nearly pulled his attention away more than once.

"It's not easy playing here on Arthur Ashe. You're playing in front of all your favorite athletes and movie stars," Shelton said after the match . "So to be able to keep your head down and focus for over three hours is not an easy task. I keep on looking up at the screen like, oh shoot, Jalen Brunson 's here."

Brunson was among a stacked list of names in attendance for the all-American semifinal. The Knicks captain, fresh off leading New York to its first NBA championship in 53 years and taking home Finals MVP honors, sat near longtime Knicks superfan Ben Stiller. Tennis legend Serena Williams was also in the building, along with actors Salma Hayek and Rami Malek and US women's soccer star Trinity Rodman, who is Shelton's girlfriend .

Despite the distractions, Shelton delivered when it mattered. After dropping a sloppy opening set in which he committed 14 unforced errors to Tiafoe's three, he leaned harder on his serve and finished with 20 aces and 47 winners. The turning point came in a grueling 19-point game to break Tiafoe and close out the third set, and Tiafoe never fully recovered from there.

The win carries enormous weight beyond Shelton's own career. He becomes the first Black American man to reach a US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972, and a victory Sunday would make him the first American man to win a major since Andy Roddick at the 2003 US Open, a drought that started before Shelton turned one. He is already guaranteed to climb to No. 4 in the world after entering the tournament ranked ninth.

Standing in his way is top seed Alexander Zverev , who is a perfect 5-0 against Shelton and has taken the past 10 sets between them, though the two have never met at a Grand Slam. If Shelton can handle the crowd the way he handled Tiafoe, he will have a chance to end 23 years of waiting for American men's tennis.

articles.title: Braves’ 31-Year-Old Pitcher Becomes Free Agent After DFA
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves designated right-hander Elieser Hernandez for assignment on September 9. The club got the resolution, as the 31-year-old cleared waivers a...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves designated right-hander Elieser Hernandez for assignment on September 9. The club got the resolution, as the 31-year-old cleared waivers and rejected an outright assignment to Triple-A Gwinnett. He is now a free agent.

Hernandez has more or less served as an additional arm when the Braves have needed someone to eat innings. The right-hander has more transactions than appearances with the club.

The 31-year-old has pitched in four games with Atlanta this season. He has a 2.45 ERA in 11 innings with 11 strikeouts and six walks. The home runs have been an issue, with all three runs he's allowed coming on solo home runs.

Elieser Hernandez Becomes Free Agent for Third Time in 2026

This is not a new development for both the Braves and Hernandez. This is the third time the right-hander has been bumped off the roster by Atlanta this season.

In his previous two runs through the waiver wire, he elected free agency over an outright assignment. What will most likely happen is that the right-hander will agree to sign another minor league deal with the Braves.

Once he agrees to another minor league deal, he should report to Gwinnett. Then, once an opportunity opens up, he could get another call-up.

Depending on how the season goes, Hernandez could find himself back in the Braves bullpen again. There may come a period where the club chooses to rest its top relievers after clinching the National League East division.

The Braves picked up a huge win over the Philadelphia Phillies and are now 87-61 on the season. Their 6-5 win in 11 innings over their division rival puts them five games up over the Phillies for the division lead. Their magic number to clinch is down to nine.

Atlanta still has two more games left against the Phillies, both presenting opportunities to bury their division rival. With a little more than two weeks left, the Braves are in a commanding position in the NL East.

There isn't much of a chance to catch up to the Los Angeles Dodgers . The Dodgers are on an eight-game winning streak and are up four games in the loss column over the Braves. Once Atlanta clinches the division, it will be about resting guys and getting them ready for the postseason.

articles.title: The Santos side that silenced La Bombonera
articles.summary: Gabriel Pierin, from the Memory CenterOn the night of September 11, 1963, a Wednesday, Santos walked into La Bombonera in front of 85,000 Boca Juniors suppor...
articles.body:
On the night of September 11 , 1963, a Wednesday, Santos walked into La Bombonera in front of 85,000 Boca Juniors supporters. It was a fanatical crowd, pushing the Argentine side in search of an unprecedented title. The match also set a new revenue record for football games in the Americas: 120,000 dollars.

There were plenty of reasons for the Argentinians to believe in the title. In the first leg of the Copa Libertadores final, at the Maracanã, Santos went 3–0 up, with two goals from Coutinho and one from Lima. In the closing minutes, however, Sanfilippo scored twice and cut the lead to 3–2. The result kept Boca alive and turned La Bombonera into a boiling cauldron.

As the 1962 Libertadores champion, Santos entered directly into the semifinal. Their opponent was Botafogo, clear leader of a group that included Alianza Lima of Peru and Millonarios of Colombia . Santos and Botafogo formed the backbone of the Brazilian National Team at that year's World Cup, and the Rio club had finished as Brazilian runner-up, behind Peixe.

In the first meeting, at Pacaembu, Santos struggled to secure a 1–1 draw, with Pelé scoring in the 45th minute of the second half. At the Maracanã, however, in front of more than 44,000 spectators, the team from Vila Belmiro gave their opponents no chance: 4–0, with three goals from Pelé and one from Lima.

On the other side was Boca Juniors, Argentine champions and Libertadores debutants. In the group stage, the Argentinians got past Olimpia of Paraguay and Universidad de Chile. In the semifinal, they defeated the mighty Peñarol, Uruguayan champions, with two wins.

The 3–2 defeat at the Maracanã made the tension for the decisive match even greater. The pressure was enormous, the pitch was in terrible condition, and Santos would need to withstand a hostile atmosphere to conquer the continent once again.

Without Mengálvio, coach Lula made changes to the team. Lima was moved into midfield, Dalmo took the right-back spot, and Geraldino came in on the left. Santos started with Gylmar, Dalmo, Mauro, Calvet and Geraldino; Lima and Zito; Dorval, Coutinho, Pelé and Pepe.

Boca, coached by Aristóbolo Deambrosi, lined up with Errea, Magdalena, Orlando Peçanha and Simeone; Rattin and Silveira; Grillo, Menéndez, Rojas, Sanfilippo and González. The match was refereed by Frenchman Marcel Albert Bois.

Needing to win, Boca went on the attack from the opening minutes. Gylmar, in great form, was forced to work hard and made a series of important saves. Santos also found space, and Pelé came close to scoring, but was stopped violently. The referee kept control of the situation and booked the offender.

The first half ended goalless. Santos controlled the game, while Boca tried to turn the pressure from the stands into an advantage on the pitch.

Right in the first minute of the second half, Grillo crossed into the area. Gylmar and Mauro got in each other's way trying to intercept the ball, which fell to Sanfilippo. The Argentine forward controlled it and struck with his right foot into the net.

La Bombonera erupted. At 1–0, the final would go to a third match. Santos only needed a draw. And the response came immediately. Three minutes later, Dorval intercepted a poorly taken goal kick by Errea and played it to Pelé. The King looked up and spotted Coutinho breaking between the center-backs. The striker received it and hit a low, firm shot into the corner. Santos goal.

The Argentine celebration lasted only three minutes. The equalizer restored control of the match to Peixe and changed the atmosphere inside La Bombonera. Mauro marshaled the defense with assurance. Lima delivered a brilliant performance in support, while Dalmo and Geraldino were helped by Dorval and Pepe in containing the runs of Grillo and González. Up front, Coutinho and Pelé began to find spaces to torment the Argentine defense.

Then, in the 37th minute, came the decisive blow. Coutinho received the ball on the left wing, moved forward, cut inside and found Pelé at the edge of the box. Surrounded by three opponents, the King slipped the ball through Orlando Peçanha's legs and, as Errea came out, poked it into the back of the net. It was Santos's second goal. For a moment, La Bombonera fell silent. Pelé was immediately surrounded by his teammates. And something rare happened that night: the greatest player in the world was applauded by the entire stadium, including part of the relentless home crowd, won over by the genius of the King of Football.

Santos beat Boca Juniors 2–1, conquered the continent once again, and secured the right to play for the world title against Milan , the European champions. Another historic battle would follow. Against the Italians, Santos would produce one of the most spectacular comebacks in its history. But that is another story. One among so many unforgettable dates in the unmatched history of Santos Futebol Clube.

articles.title: Santos FC and Umbro unveil new third kit for the season
articles.summary: Santos FC and Umbro, the Club’s official sponsor, are launching the Club’s new third kit for the season. Built around the concept “Go with determination,” on...
articles.body:
Santos FC and Umbro, the Club's official sponsor, are launching the Club's new third kit for the season . Built around the concept "Go with determination," one of the chants sung by the fans in the stands, the jersey seeks to revive elements from a season marked by the strength, resilience, and fighting spirit of the Santos side.

The inspiration comes from the 1997 kit, a year in which Santos FC fielded a team of widely recognized technical quality and built its journey throughout the season with determination in the face of challenges. The new kit transforms that spirit into a contemporary reinterpretation, connecting memory and tradition with a more modern visual proposal.

"The launch of the number 3 kit strengthens Santos FC's connection with its history and with a period of great emotion. More than that, it reinforces its bond with the fans and with a chant that represents encouragement and motivation for our players. The phrase 'Go with determination' has been part of great victories and historic comebacks. Santos FC and Umbro have maintained a long partnership, focused on the club and especially on our fans. In practice, it is a tribute to and recognition of the strength that comes from the stands. It will certainly be another success story," said Marcelo Teixeira, president of Santos FC.

Predominantly black, the jersey embraces a low-contrast aesthetic and a minimalist look, with white details and a jacquard fabric that combines matte and glossy finishes. The effect creates a subtle texture throughout the garment and reinforces the model's refined proposal.

One of the main highlights is the modern reinterpretation of the crest used by Santos FC in 1997, an element that creates a direct link to the kit's historical inspiration. In the Player version, the crest is applied in TPU, while the version intended for fans uses a woven application.

"Santos is a club that built its history with talent, personality, and a constant ability to overcome challenges. In this third kit, we sought to look to the past and recover values such as resilience and determination, bringing that inspiration into a current, sophisticated jersey full of details that reinforce Santos's identity. It is a piece that connects different generations of fans through the club's history and tradition," said Eduardo Dal Pogetto, Umbro's director in Brazil.

The concept also appears in the garment's internal details. The customized half-moon features graphic references linked to the Santos universe, while the label located at the hem reinforces the message "Go with determination." The back of the collar also bears the expression "Resilience and determination," deepening the connection between the concept and the kit's visual construction.

With a proposal that combines historical reinterpretation, minimalism, and refinement, Santos's third kit for 2026 celebrates a trait present in different moments of the club's black-and-white history: the determination to keep moving forward and overcome adversity.

As has been the case for a few years now, a Fan version of Peixe's shirts will also be made available, arriving on the market at a lower price than the Player version. In addition to the fabric, the Fan shirt features different details on the sleeves, hem, and inside of the collars, and will be available in men's, women's, youth, and kids' models, as well as long-sleeve and tank top versions.

Founded in 1924, Umbro is the authentic football brand, having been dedicated to the sport for more than 102 years. Born in Manchester, England, Umbro has its products worn on and off the pitch in more than 100 countries around the world. Today, the company combines its heritage in sports tailoring with a modern vision of football to create apparel, footwear, and accessories that blend performance and style.

articles.title: Garcia v Benn - welterweight world title fight predictions
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's WBC welterweight world title fight between Ryan Garcia and Briton Conor Benn.
articles.body:
Conor Benn returns to welterweight for the first time since April 2022 to challenge WBC champion Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas.

The 29-year-old Briton is bidding for the crowning moment of his 10-year professional career at T-Mobile Arena.

Benn has won 25 of his 26 fights as a professional and would emulate his father, Nigel, by claiming a WBC title with another victory.

Garcia, 28, is making the first defence of his belt after beating Mario Barrios by decision in February.

The American has picked up 25 victories in his 28-fight career, earning 20 of those wins by knockout, while losing two, with one no-contest.

Live text commentary will begin on Sunday, 13 September at 03:00 BST on the BBC Sport website and app.

BBC Sport spoke to figures from the boxing world to get their predictions for the bout.

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"This is a really good fight and it's not as one-sided as everyone thinks. I believe Conor Benn's heart is going to come into question and he's going to have to climb off the floor a couple of times.

"If Garcia has taken this lightly in any way he will lose, but he's in great shape and is saying the right things in the build-up. But I'm still going for a Conor Benn knockout inside eight rounds."

Carl Frampton - former two-weight world champion

"I thought Benn had a fair chance due to his tenacity and Garcia has quit in fights before. But as the fight is getting closer I think Benn is a big underdog and it's Garcia's fight to lose.

"Benn looked terrible in a catchweight - 3lb above the welterweight limit - last time out against an ageing Regis Prograis, who was injured and had only one good leg, and he couldn't put a dent in him.

"He looks like he's struggled with the weight cut and I don't get a good feeling, so I'll go with a comfortable Garcia win."

Barry Jones - former super-featherweight world champion

"We know Benn can be tenacious and has power but I don't think he'll be the same fighter he was in the two fights against Chris Eubank Jr. Benn didn't look great in his last fight against Regis Prograis, so you have to give favour to Garcia.

"Garcia has speed, power and patience. Benn will force the pace and I think he walks on to a shot. I'll go with Garcia to get the stoppage inside five rounds."

"Benn is going to get knocked out in one or two rounds. You can't take off all this weight at this age - he doesn't even look recognisable."

Paul Smith - former world title challenger

"It's heavily on what Garcia turns up. If a very good Garcia turns up I can see it being over early."

"Conor Benn has a problem because it's at welterweight and he's had to grind down to make weight, so how will he deal with the speed, skill and power of Garcia? Benn is tenacious and fierce so I think it will be enticing. But you have to favour champion Garcia on home soil."

Anthony Crolla - former lightweight world champion

"I can't look past a Ryan Garcia knockout. I think this is a huge step up for Conor - I hope I'm wrong - but you can't compare this fight to his ones with Chris Eubank Jr. This is a gigantic step up in class."

Josh Taylor - former undisputed light-welterweight champion

"If Ryan had the right mentality and trained properly, the main word being if, I think he stops Conor Benn within six.

"If not, I think Conor gets through the 12 rounds but loses on points by a few rounds."

Kevin Iole - boxing journalist and boxing Hall of Fame inductee

"I have to pick Garcia because I think Conor is one-dimensional and the speed will be a big factor. Benn is good when the going gets tough, while Ryan is unpredictable - but if both guys are at their best then Ryan wins."

"I think Ryan Garcia gets it done - and early. Conor Benn will come out like a steam train and that could be a problem.

"Garcia has the hand speed and serious experience around the ring - he's been doing this for longer than Benn - which might be a bit too much.

"Garcia to win between rounds four and seven, but it should be a fun fight for five or six rounds."

articles.title: Buffalo Bills depth chart: Projected starting lineup vs. Texans
articles.summary: The Bills' first depth chart shows a familiar offense around Josh Allen and a revamped defense under new coordinator Jim Leonhard.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills changed head coaches for the first time in nearly a decade.

Josh Allen might barely notice when he looks around the huddle.

The other side of the ball is a different story.

Buffalo released its first unofficial depth chart ahead of Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans , giving the clearest look yet at how Joe Brady's first starting lineup could look.

The offense is mostly familiar. The defense is not.

Only two starters on offense are different from Buffalo's opening depth chart last season. The Bills could have more than twice that many changes on defense as coordinator Jim Leonhard installs a new 3-4 scheme.

The Bills visit the Texans at 1 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 13, at Reliant Stadium.

Here's a look at Buffalo's projected starting lineup, what's changed from last season and the complete depth chart.

Buffalo Bills projected starting offense vs. Texans

There are two changes to the Bills' offensive starters from a year ago.

WR: DJ Moore — The biggest change among Buffalo's skill-position starters. The Bills traded with the Chicago Bears for Moore during the offseason.

LG: Alec Anderson — Won the starting job over Austin Corbett in training camp.

Buffalo Bills projected starting defense vs. Texans

The first thing that looks different is the formation.

Buffalo is listed in a base 3-4 defense under Leonhard after playing primarily out of a four-man defensive front under Sean McDermott.

That makes a direct position-by-position comparison imperfect, but the personnel turnover is obvious.

DL: T.J. Sanders — Moves into a prominent role after being part of Buffalo's defensive tackle rotation as a rookie. He's listed as one of three starting defensive linemen.

DL: Deone Walker — Takes over in the middle of the defensive front. DaQuan Jones occupied that role in Buffalo's old defense entering last season.

OLB: Bradley Chubb — One of Buffalo's biggest offseason changes. Chubb signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract and replaces Joey Bosa as the veteran pass rusher opposite Rousseau.

LB: Dorian Williams — Steps into a full-time starting role after Matt Milano opened last season alongside Bernard.

CB: Maxwell Hairston — Listed as the starter opposite Benford after beginning his rookie season on injured reserve last year.

NB: Dee Alford — Signed a three-year, $15.75 million free-agent contract to take over the nickel job previously held by Taron Johnson . The Bills traded Johnson during the offseason.

FS: C.J. Gardner-Johnson — Replaces Taylor Rapp and gives Buffalo another veteran addition to a secondary that changed substantially during the offseason.

Buffalo Bills projected special teams starters

P/H: Tommy Doman Jr. — The Bills' rookie seventh-round pick beat out veteran Mitch Wishnowsky for the job.

PR: Dee Alford — His spot atop the punt-returner depth chart is one of the more surprising details in Buffalo's first release.

The depth chart is unofficial and injuries could still alter Buffalo's actual Week 1 lineup.

TE: Dalton Kincaid; Dawson Knox ; Jackson Hawes ; Keleki Latu

C: Connor McGovern; Lloyd Cushenberry III

RG: O'Cyrus Torrence; Ar'maj Reed-Adams; Austin Corbett

DE: T.J. Sanders; Landon Jackson ; Phidarian Mathis (suspended)

DE: Ed Oliver; DeWayne Carter ; Zane Durant (IR)

OLB: Greg Rousseau; Michael Hoecht ; Mike Danna

OLB: Bradley Chubb; TJ Parker; Javon Solomon

S: C.J. Gardner-Johnson; Damar Hamlin ; Sam Franklin Jr.

PR: Dee Alford; Ray Davis; Khalil Shakir (Q)

articles.title: 'Outstanding' star makes Liverpool hierarchy eat their words about his future
articles.summary: Liverpool have made a lot of changes to their squad this summer. Some players such as Harvey Elliott and Curtis Jones have been moved on, while others, such...
articles.body:
Liverpool have made a lot of changes to their squad this summer.

Some players such as Harvey Elliott and Curtis Jones have been moved on , while others, such as Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet have been brought in.

It's not just their playing staff what have changed either with a decent chunk of the Reds' backroom staff also being re-jigged.

Richard Hughes is now Al-Hilal's sporting director and Michael Edwards just decided to quit after Fenway Sports Group's multi-club model was thrown in the bin.

Even though all these changes have been made, it still feels like more needs to be done before Liverpool are ready to be seen as genuine contenders for the Premier League title again.

And, with the sheer number of contracts that are set to expire over the next couple of years, it's clear that a lot more re-jigging is on its way to Anfield.

However, for one Liverpool star, it feels like he's made a mockery of Liverpool after the decision that they made about his future.

Alexis Mac Allister has been told that he isn't good enough for a new Liverpool contract

Alexis Mac Allister 's contract may not expire until 2028 but, with the way that things have gone for Liverpool over the last couple of years, locking down the future's of any players with any sort of value is going to be key to their survival.

Recently, Trent Alexander-Arnold , Ibrahima Konate, Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson have all left L4 for nothing.

Obviously, some players such as Robertson and Salah may not have had all that much value left within them but, it still sucks for the Reds to have lost them for nothing.

And, since Jones' contract was going to expire at the end of the current campaign, he was also moved on for a cut-rate fee.

This is a pattern that Liverpool can't continue to follow but, as per an update from BBC Sport, it seems like Liverpool didn't think that Mac Allister was anywhere near good enough to earn a new contract.

"The understanding is the powers that be at Liverpool were of the belief that Mac Allister's performances did not warrant the offer of fresh terms," they wrote .

"But if he can carry on like this, then it will be a question of when rather than if that offer is made for whoever replaces Richard Hughes - even if Mac Allister said he didn't know if his goal would boost his chances of a new contract."

Alexis Mac Allister has already proven that Liverpool are wrong about their assumptions

Over the last few weeks, it's clear that Andoni Iraola has been trying to figure out what his best XI actually is.

Cody Gakpo has been used on the right-wing and, the Reds' midfield has been changed around more times than anyone can remember.

From an outside perspective, it felt obvious that Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch would be Liverpool's starting midfielders.

However, after their opening game as a pair against Newcastle, it was clear that it wasn't going to work out.

So, this has led to Mac Allister being given a more prominent role than anyone expected and, if we're being honest, he's exceeded the expectations of everyone.

Last term, the Argentinian performed well below his usual standards with fans even demanding that he got sold.

However, that didn't end up happening which is why it's now a bit of a shock to see him becoming one of Liverpool's best players.

His determination on the pitch has been second-to-none and, his goal against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday evening was stunning.

If he continues performing to this level, he'll certainly end up making Liverpool re-think their stance on the " outstanding " midfielders future, even if a renewal is likely to cost them an arm and a leg.
